hero.title: PDF-to-Word & Document Conversion Services
hero.lead: PDF conversion, OCR and editable document preparation for publishers, localization service providers and translation agencies.
paragraphs: EPUBTRANS provides document and data conversion services to help organizations transform PDFs, scanned documents and other source materials into editable or structured files for further use.
Our services include PDF-to-Word conversion, OCR-assisted text extraction, document reconstruction, formatting cleanup and preparation of files for publishing, editing and localization workflows.

Whether you need to recreate a non-editable PDF, extract content from scanned pages or prepare documents for translation, we can review your source files and define an appropriate conversion approach.

sections.title: Document Conversion for Publishing & Localization Workflows

lead.text: Many publishing and localization projects begin with source documents that are difficult to edit or reuse.

A PDF may contain selectable text but lack usable formatting. A scanned document may contain only page images. Complex layouts can include columns, tables, graphics and text boxes that do not convert cleanly into editable files.
Document conversion helps prepare these materials for their next production stage.
EPUBTRANS supports conversion requirements based on the condition of the source files, intended output format and agreed editing or layout specifications.

blocks.text: Converting PDF content into Microsoft Word can make text available for editing, formatting and downstream production.
Depending on the source file, the work may include:

items: Restoring headers, footers and page elements
Placing or extracting images and figures

blocks.text: The amount of reconstruction required depends on whether the PDF contains usable text, has a consistent structure and includes recoverable document elements.
A PDF-to-Word conversion may prioritize editable content, layout similarity or a combination of the two. These requirements should be clarified before production.
Optical character recognition (OCR) can be used to extract text from scanned pages and image-based documents.
OCR output may require review and correction, especially when source documents contain low-resolution text, unusual fonts, multiple columns, technical symbols or inconsistent page quality.
Depending on the project, OCR-related activities may include text extraction, content cleanup, structure reconstruction and preparation of an agreed editable output.
OCR recognition alone does not guarantee complete or correct text extraction.
When the original editable source file is unavailable, document elements may need to be recreated from a PDF or other reference.
The work can involve rebuilding text frames, headings, tables, illustrations, page numbering and other layout features.
Depending on the requirements and technical feasibility, reconstructed content may be prepared in Word, PowerPoint, InDesign or another agreed target format.
The feasibility of recreating the original design depends on source quality, fonts, graphics and the limitations of the selected output format.
Conversion of suitable content into documents that can be edited and reused.
Depending on the agreed scope, this may include preparing editable text, applying styles, rebuilding sections and organizing document elements for further production.
OCR-assisted extraction and reconstruction of scanned documents.
Documents with skewed pages, faint text, poor contrast, handwritten content or complex structures may require additional assessment and manual work.
Recreating tables, figures and related document elements when they need to remain editable or follow an agreed structure.
For complex tables, diagrams or equations, the required output should be clarified because certain elements may need specialist reconstruction or may remain as images.
Reviewing and correcting formatting issues introduced by extraction or conversion.
Work may include resolving unnecessary line breaks, inconsistent spacing, misplaced text, paragraph formatting and other structural problems within the agreed scope.
Rebuilding document layouts from available PDFs or reference files.
This may involve reproducing headings, text flow, columns, page elements and supporting assets according to the client's layout requirements.
Preparing documents for use in publishing, localization or other agreed content workflows.
Requirements may involve editable files, consistent text structure, output format compatibility or layout references for later production stages.
Specialist eBook conversion, XML markup, accessibility remediation and multilingual DTP are handled as separate services when those activities are required.

lead.text: Localization service providers and translation agencies often receive documents that are difficult to process in their existing translation workflows.
For example, a project may begin with a PDF rather than the original editable Word or layout file. Scanned content may require OCR, while tables and text boxes may need to be reconstructed.
EPUBTRANS can assess these files and prepare agreed editable outputs for downstream localization work.

blocks.text: The conversion process may involve extracting text, rebuilding document structure and preparing content in an editable format.
The target output can be defined according to the localization team's requirements.
Where required, document preparation may focus on consistent text structure, paragraph styles, tables and other elements relevant to later processing.
Compatibility with a particular computer-assisted translation (CAT) tool or translation management system must be reviewed separately.
Document conversion does not automatically include translation, linguistic proofreading, terminology management or post-translation desktop publishing.
EPUBTRANS can assess related production requirements, but the activities and responsibilities should be agreed before work begins.
Discuss Your Document Conversion Requirements

sections.title: Document Conversion for Publishers & Content Teams

lead.text: Publishers may need to transform existing content into files that can be edited, repurposed or prepared for additional production activities.
Typical situations include:

items: Converting legacy PDFs into editable documents
Reconstructing source files when originals are unavailable
Preparing publication content for editorial review
Rebuilding tables and structured document elements
Preparing source content for typesetting or digital publishing

lead.text: Existing publications can vary considerably in source quality and technical complexity.
Projects involving structured XML, EPUB conversion or complete publication typesetting should be assessed for the appropriate specialist workflow.
Not every conversion project has the same intended outcome.
Before production begins, it is important to establish which characteristics of the source document must be retained.

blocks.text: The priority is to make the text and required document elements available for editing or reuse.
The converted document may have a simpler layout than the original when visual similarity is not essential.
The priority is to recreate the source document's visual arrangement as closely as is feasible within the chosen output format.
This may require additional formatting, manual reconstruction and attention to fonts, tables, images and pagination.
Some projects require both editable content and substantial visual similarity to the source.
These projects may involve more reconstruction than basic text extraction.
Exact pagination, fully editable graphic elements or identical rendering across applications cannot be assumed without reviewing the source document and output requirements.

sections.title: Source Files & Materials We Can Assess

lead.text: The source file, available assets and target output influence the conversion workflow.

items: Existing editable documents requiring format changes
Reference layouts or approved sample files
Supporting graphics, tables or other document assets

blocks.text: Please provide the following where available:

items: Approximate page count or file volume
Required output format and application version
Whether editability or visual similarity is the main priority
Language and script information where relevant
Requirements for tables, figures, equations and images

blocks.text: For longer or technically complex documents, a representative sample can help determine whether additional extraction, reconstruction or review work is required.

lead.text: Deliverables are defined according to the agreed project requirements.

blocks.text: DOCX files containing the converted and reconstructed content, with applicable formatting and structural elements.
Text extracted from digital or scanned sources, in an agreed file format.
Additional cleanup or structural preparation should be included explicitly in the scope.
Word, PowerPoint, InDesign or other agreed editable formats where technically suitable and supported.
Documents prepared with the agreed headings, paragraphs, tables, images and other layout elements.
Related assets and conversion outputs organized according to the specified delivery requirements.
Where appropriate, the delivery package can identify known exclusions, unresolved source issues or limitations affecting particular document elements.
We review the supplied documents, source quality, file structure, language requirements and intended output.
Potential challenges such as scanned text, missing fonts, complex tables or image-based content are identified.
We clarify the required target format, degree of editability, layout expectations, content-review requirements and delivery specifications.
For complex source files, a sample assessment may be recommended before confirming the complete production scope.
The appropriate extraction, OCR, formatting or reconstruction activities are performed according to the agreed requirements.
Manual preparation may be included for content that cannot be converted satisfactorily through automated processing alone.
Relevant content, formatting and structural checks are performed according to the project specification.
Issues identified through the agreed review process are addressed within the defined correction scope.
Completed files and associated assets are prepared in the agreed format and package structure.
The final deliverables reflect the approved output specifications and any documented exclusions.

lead.text: Conversion quality depends on the original source and the acceptance criteria for the target output.
Depending on the project, checks may cover:

items: Visual comparison with the original document

blocks.text: Document conversion checks focus on transferring and reconstructing source content correctly according to the agreed requirements.
They do not automatically include copyediting, linguistic proofreading, factual verification or correction of errors already present in the source.
OCR is particularly sensitive to the condition of scanned material.
Some projects may require additional manual comparison, text correction or specialized handling of equations and symbols.
The required review method and acceptance criteria should be agreed before production.

sections.title: What Affects Document Conversion Scope & Schedule?

blocks.text: Clean, searchable PDFs may be easier to process than scanned documents with blurred, skewed or low-resolution pages.
Multi-column documents, extensive tables, forms, mathematical content and embedded graphics can require additional work.
Extracting usable text is different from reconstructing an editable document containing native tables, styles and other elements.
Maintaining visual similarity can require additional formatting and manual reconstruction.
The language, writing system, fonts, symbols and source encoding can influence extraction and formatting requirements.
The number of files, page count, expected output formats, correction rounds and requested quality checks can affect production effort.
We review these factors before confirming scope, estimated cost or delivery arrangements.

lead.text: Document conversion may be one stage in a broader content-production workflow.

blocks.text: Multilingual formatting, post-translation DTP and layout adaptation for documents that require target-language production.
Book and journal page composition where manuscript content needs to be prepared for publication.
EPUB production and eBook conversion for suitable publishing content.
Specialist XML article markup for scholarly publications requiring SciELO-related workflows.
Accessibility-related remediation and preparation for supported document and digital publishing formats.
These services can be commissioned separately or assessed together where the project requirements call for connected production activities.

groups.title: Can EPUBTRANS convert PDF files into editable Word documents?

blocks.text: PDF-to-Word conversion is part of EPUBTRANS's documented service scope. The degree of editability and layout reconstruction depends on the source file and agreed output requirements.

groups.title: Can you convert scanned PDFs into Word documents?

blocks.text: Scanned PDFs can be assessed for OCR-assisted conversion and reconstruction. Source quality, text recognition, formatting complexity and review requirements affect the production approach.

groups.title: Will the converted Word file look exactly like the original PDF?

blocks.text: Not necessarily. Exact visual reproduction and editable content are separate requirements. The level of layout similarity should be confirmed after examining representative source files.

groups.title: Can you recreate tables, images and diagrams?

blocks.text: Tables, figures and document elements can be assessed for extraction or reconstruction. Some may require manual work, while others may need to remain as images depending on the agreed output.

groups.title: Do you provide conversion files suitable for translation?

blocks.text: EPUBTRANS can prepare editable documents for localization workflows. Requirements involving CAT-tool compatibility, segmentation, language processing and translation-system testing must be confirmed separately.

groups.title: Do you support OCR for multiple languages?

blocks.text: Language-specific OCR projects can be assessed. The supported languages, scripts, recognition methods and correction requirements need to be confirmed before production.

groups.title: Can you recreate a document in InDesign or PowerPoint?

blocks.text: The documented service catalog includes reconstruction into Word, PowerPoint, InDesign or another agreed target when technically suitable. Current software compatibility and file-format requirements must be checked for each project.
OCR-related content checking may be included according to the agreed specification. Full linguistic proofreading or editorial correction is not automatically part of document conversion.

groups.title: Can you convert legacy publishing files?

blocks.text: Eligible legacy documents can be assessed according to the available source files and desired output. Support for specific legacy software or file versions must be confirmed.

groups.title: Do you provide XML or EPUB conversion as part of this service?

blocks.text: EPUBTRANS offers related XML and EPUB production services, but these are scoped separately when specialist publishing requirements apply.

groups.title: What information is required for a document conversion quote?

blocks.text: Please provide representative source files, approximate page or file volume, target output format, editing and layout requirements, language information where relevant, and the preferred schedule.

groups.title: Can EPUBTRANS handle a large volume of documents?

blocks.text: Projects involving multiple files or substantial document volumes can be reviewed for feasibility, resource requirements and delivery planning. Capacity and schedules are confirmed only after assessment.
